emails.subject: See how Plausible reports traffic without cookies
emails.single_idea: Cyrus Shepard, an SEO consultant and former Moz lead, described Plausible as easy to use with near-real-time data; inspect the live dashboard to decide whether that reporting experience merits a closer evaluation by your team.
emails.selection_reason: A named analytics practitioner described Plausible as easy to use with near-real-time data. That assessment is a concrete but limited reason for a government digital team to inspect the live dashboard and form its own view before considering a formal evaluation.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Plausible's dashboard appears clear and relevant enough to include in a formal analytics evaluation.
emails.next_step_value: The destination provides a live example dashboard for first-hand inspection, allowing the reader to assess the reporting experience behind Shepard's limited description of the product as easy to use with near-real-time data.
emails.next_step_limit: The demo does not establish fit for specific reporting views or explorations, government-scale API workloads, procurement or compliance approval, accessibility, historical-data comparison, custom-data limits, implementation effort or production use.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: A web analytics service that would replace or supplement our traffic reporting with a lightweight, cookie-free script and a single near-real-time dashboard.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The profile explicitly establishes that our public-sector team must run analytics without a consent banner, so the email's claim of analytics without cookies or personal-data collection is directly relevant. The profile also documents reporting difficulties experienced by some government teams using GA4, but it does not establish that our team uses GA4, has those difficulties, or is currently evaluating a replacement. The email appropriately offers inspection rather than assuming an active procurement, although it does not connect its privacy claims to the specific no-banner requirement.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: we need to publish web analytics without a consent banner.
Email-only: we may be considering Plausible for a formal evaluation.
Email-only: a single, lightweight analytics dashboard may be relevant to our reporting needs.
Not established by the profile: that we currently use GA4, GTM or Universal Analytics.
Not established by the profile: that we have personally encountered GA4 reporting, quota, historical-comparison, storage-cost or character-limit problems.
reader_verdicts.problem_now: Consent-free analytics is a current, documented requirement for this audience. Whether our present setup fails that requirement, whether GA4-related reporting problems affect us, and whether an evaluation is timely are unknown.
reader_verdicts.stopped_at: Cyrus Shepard, an SEO consultant and former Moz lead, described Plausible as easy to use, with near-real-time data.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: I cannot tell whether "without cookies or collecting personal data" is sufficient to operate without a consent banner under our legal and governance requirements, or whether the dashboard can meet public-sector reporting needs beyond basic traffic figures.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me whether the live demo shows the specific evidence needed to assess consent-banner requirements and government reporting needs, such as data fields, journey analysis, exports and retention.
fixes: Cut "Cyrus Shepard, an SEO consultant and former Moz lead, described Plausible as easy to use, with near-real-time data." The opinion of an SEO practitioner does not answer a public-sector team's privacy, governance or reporting questions.

Rewrite "Plausible is privacy-friendly web analytics that measures site traffic with one lightweight script and one dashboard, without cookies or collecting personal data." as "Plausible is web analytics delivered through one lightweight script and dashboard; the live demo shows the data collected, reporting views and export options so you can assess whether its cookie-free approach could meet your consent and governance requirements."

Rewrite "You can see how its reporting is organised and make a limited first decision: whether the experience appears clear and relevant enough for your team to evaluate further." as "Use the live demo to inspect the available metrics, filters, journey reporting and exports before deciding whether a formal technical, legal and accessibility review is worthwhile."
Rewrite "View the live demo →" as "Inspect the live dashboard—no signup required →" if no signup is genuinely required; otherwise state the actual access step.
reader_verdicts.persona:
Selected audience (explicit constraints): An EU or UK public sector web team that must publish analytics without a consent banner.
The context and problem reports below describe observed members of this market, not established experiences or installed tools of this recipient. The campaign request controls which job this email addresses; do not require a link to an unrequested integration in your doubts or click requirements.
Observed context (grounded; applicability must be checked): Digital teams running national and devolved UK government web services (such as GOV.UK/GDS and Scottish Government Design System sites) operate web analytics tooling built on Google Analytics/GA4 and Google Tag Manager as part of normal service operation, and are in the middle of migrating from Universal Analytics to GA4.
Source: https://gds.blog.gov.uk/2023/03/27/sharing-data-and-lessons-from-our-google-analytics-4-upgrade/; quote: We’ve also been comparing our UA and GA4 data sources and using GA4 data in reports and dashboards.
Source: https://designsystem.gov.scot/guidance/analytics; quote: Scottish Government Design System sites primarily use Google Tag Manager (GTM) and Google Analytics (GA).
Problem context: GOV.UK found that the GA4 reporting interface — including its lack of multiple reporting views and issues with reports/explorations — does not meet their needs the way Universal Analytics did.; source: https://gds.blog.gov.uk/2023/03/27/sharing-data-and-lessons-from-our-google-analytics-4-upgrade/
Problem context: GOV.UK's use of the GA4 API for tools such as Looker Studio is constrained by strict API quota limits.; source: https://gds.blog.gov.uk/2023/03/27/sharing-data-and-lessons-from-our-google-analytics-4-upgrade/
Problem context: GA4's changed definitions of core concepts (such as sessions) and its batching of events make it hard for GOV.UK to compare GA4 data with their historical Universal Analytics data and to plot user journeys.; source: https://gds.blog.gov.uk/2023/03/27/sharing-data-and-lessons-from-our-google-analytics-4-upgrade/
Problem context: GOV.UK expects GA4's larger daily data tables to increase their data storage costs compared with Universal Analytics.; source: https://gds.blog.gov.uk/2023/03/27/sharing-data-and-lessons-from-our-google-analytics-4-upgrade/
Problem context: Character limits on data sent to GA4 constrain what GOV.UK is able to collect.; source: https://gds.blog.gov.uk/2023/03/27/sharing-data-and-lessons-from-our-google-analytics-4-upgrade/
Qualified scope of the selected audience: Devolved and national government digital teams. This narrows who you are; it does not establish installed tools, prior actions or desired reactions.

The email does not assume that we use Plausible, are switching tools, or have begun an evaluation. assets.title: See how Plausible reports traffic without cookies
assets.content:
Subject: See how Plausible reports traffic without cookies
Preview text: The live example shows its dashboard and near-real-time reporting in practice.

Hi there,

You can inspect Plausible Analytics’ live dashboard before deciding whether it belongs in a formal evaluation.

Plausible is privacy-friendly web analytics that measures site traffic with one lightweight script and one dashboard, without cookies or collecting personal data.

Cyrus Shepard, an SEO consultant and former Moz lead, described Plausible as easy to use, with near-real-time data. That is one practitioner’s assessment, not evidence that the product will meet a government team’s reporting requirements.

The live example lets you examine the dashboard directly. You can see how its reporting is organised and make a limited first decision: whether the experience appears clear and relevant enough for your team to evaluate further.

View the live demo → https://plausible.io/plausible.io

- the Plausible Analytics team

report.audience_scope: Devolved and national government digital teams
report.assessment_method: Simulated editorial assessment, uncalibrated; no response or conversion prediction

emails.subject: Inspect a cookie-free analytics dashboard
emails.single_idea: A government web team can evaluate Plausible as a cookie-free analytics option without first taking claims about reporting usefulness on trust: the live dashboard shows the traffic sources, pages and goals it reports.
emails.selection_reason: The no-cookie design directly matches this audience's consent constraint, while the live dashboard gives an unknown reader a concrete way to determine whether Plausible provides useful core analytics before beginning assurance or procurement work.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Plausible's core dashboard is relevant enough to enter the team's formal analytics, privacy and procurement assessment.
emails.next_step_value: The public demo lets the reader inspect a working dashboard showing live traffic sources, pages being viewed and goals being met without creating an account.
emails.next_step_limit: The demo does not establish fit for department-specific reporting, API workloads, historical-data requirements, accessibility review, DPIA approval, procurement, SSO or production implementation.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: Plausible sells a cookie-free web analytics service, and the immediate offer is a no-account demo I could inspect to see whether its traffic, page and goal reporting merits a formal assessment.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The profile explicitly establishes that my team must publish analytics without a consent banner, so a cookie-free analytics service is directly relevant. The email additionally claims that Plausible collects no personal data and uses no persistent or cross-site identifiers; those are vendor claims, not established facts about the product or my circumstances. Whether its reporting, governance and technical controls meet public-sector requirements remains unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I work in an EU or UK public-sector web team that needs analytics without a consent banner.
Email-only: my services need traffic-source, page and goal reporting in the form demonstrated.
Email-only: basic dashboard reporting is the main question my team needs to resolve before a formal assessment.
Not established: that my team currently uses GA4, GTM or any particular analytics product.
Not established: that my team is actively replacing its current analytics tooling or has time allocated for an assessment.
reader_verdicts.problem_now: Consent-free analytics is a documented requirement for this audience, so the category matters now. The adequacy of Plausible's reporting and the urgency of evaluating a replacement are unknown; the observed GA4 problems may be relevant, but the profile does not establish that my particular team experiences them.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: The dashboard is easy to inspect, but the consequential privacy claims are merely asserted. I cannot tell whether “no personal data” is supported by documentation suitable for an EU or UK public-sector assessment, including the basis for operating without a consent banner.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me that the demo also links directly to the technical and legal documentation supporting the no-personal-data and no-consent-banner claims.
fixes: Rewrite “Plausible is a web analytics service that uses no cookies and collects no personal data.” as “Plausible is a web analytics service that uses no cookies; the demo and linked technical documentation show what is collected so your privacy team can assess whether it can operate without a consent banner.”

Rewrite “The public demo provides a working view of its core reporting without requiring an account.” as “The public demo requires no account and lets you check traffic sources, pages and goals; it also links to the data-collection and privacy documentation needed for an initial assessment.”

Cut “It is a concrete way to judge whether cookie-free analytics can provide the basic traffic, page and goal information your services need.” because it repeats the preceding explanation without answering the assurance question.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: A cookie-free web analytics service whose public dashboard I can inspect to see how it reports traffic sources, page views and goals before considering a formal assessment.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The premise directly matches the profile-supported requirement to publish analytics without a consent banner. The email clearly offers a no-account demo, so the immediate step is proportionate. However, the profile does not establish that our team uses GA4, needs these specific three reports, or is currently selecting a replacement; those remain unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: our public-sector web team must publish analytics without a consent banner.
Email-only: traffic sources, page views and goals are the core information our services need.
Email-only: we are deciding whether to begin a formal privacy and reporting assessment of another analytics service.
Unknown applicability from the market context: our team currently uses GA4 or GTM and experiences the documented reporting, quota, historical-comparison, storage or character-limit problems.
reader_verdicts.problem_now: Consent-free analytics is an explicit current constraint, so the category is relevant now. The cited GA4 problems matter in this market, but whether they affect our team or create current replacement urgency is unknown.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: The consequential claims that the service collects no personal data and can therefore support cookie-free analytics are asserted without any technical or legal basis; a dashboard demo can show reporting, but it cannot validate those claims.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me the specific technical basis for the claim that no personal data is collected under UK/EU privacy requirements.
fixes: Rewrite “Plausible is a web analytics service that uses no cookies and collects no personal data.” to state the specific collection method and the basis on which the sender concludes that the collected data is not personal data.

Rewrite “It also uses no persistent identifiers or cross-site or cross-device tracking, and does not reuse site data for other purposes.” to identify what data is retained, for how long, and for which defined purposes.

Replace “It is a concrete way to judge whether cookie-free analytics can provide the basic traffic, page and goal information your services need.” with “Use the demo to judge whether its traffic-source, page and goal reports meet your reporting requirements; privacy and governance claims would still require separate assessment.”

assets.title: Inspect a cookie-free analytics dashboard
assets.content:
Subject: Inspect a cookie-free analytics dashboard
Preview text: See the traffic sources, pages and goals Plausible reports in its public demo.

Hi there,

You can inspect Plausible Analytics’ live dashboard before deciding whether it belongs in a formal privacy and reporting assessment. It shows where traffic comes from, which pages are being viewed and which goals are being met.

Plausible is a web analytics service that uses no cookies and collects no personal data. It also uses no persistent identifiers or cross-site or cross-device tracking, and does not reuse site data for other purposes.

The public demo provides a working view of its core reporting without requiring an account. Your team can compare the dashboard with its own requirements before committing time to a fuller assessment.

It is a concrete way to judge whether cookie-free analytics can provide the basic traffic, page and goal information your services need.

View the live demo → https://plausible.io/plausible.io

- the Plausible Analytics team
